stories.title: Flights resume at Riyadh airport after two-week closure as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
summary: Flights resumed at Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday following a series of deadly attacks on the facility that saw it closed for two weeks, even as Yemen’s Houthi rebels targeted the country with strikes.

Alerts warning of possible attacks were activated across the kingdom’s south throughout the day, with the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis saying at least 10 ballistic missiles were intercepted.
The attacks came after the Houthi fighters said that — in the space of 24 hours — they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.

stories.title: KP Governor Kundi says Sohail Afridi, assembly speaker 'in safe hands' after house arrest
summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Sunday that Sohail Afridi and Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were “in safe hands” after being placed under house arrest.

Appearing on Geo News’ TV programme ‘Jirga’ aired on Sunday night, the governor — who now runs the province — was asked about the whereabouts of Afridi, Kundi said he had been placed under house arrest and was “in safe hands — there is no need to worry”.
Asked why Afridi was not being released if there were no cases against him, Kundi replied he could provide an update tomorrow regarding the matter.

stories.title: Shadab Khan’s match-winning century sparks social media celebrations after Pakistan’s thrilling win
summary: Social media was awash with praise on Sunday after Shadab Khan struck an unbeaten century to steer Pakistan to a dramatic one-wicket victory over England in the fourth match of the One-day International tri-series at the Gaddafi Stadium.

Chasing 242, Pakistan were in deep trouble at 154-9 before Shadab’s 113 not out off 96 balls, featuring 13 fours and five sixes, and an unbroken 89-run partnership with Haris Rauf turned the match on its head.
The victory secured Pakistan’s place in the tri-series final and set a record for the highest 10th-wicket partnership in a successful ODI chase.

stories.title: Billionaire Trump backer Bill Ackman says Ben-Gvir, Smotrich should not serve in next Israeli govt
summary: Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman on Sunday said that Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel’s next government, saying the two far-right politicians had caused enormous damage to the country’s reputation.

Ackman wrote on X that from the perspective of someone who had an understanding of how Israel was perceived in the United States, “Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have caused Israel enormous reputational damage with their statements and actions”.

As ministers in Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have overseen policies widely perceived as discriminatory against Israel’s minority Arab population and Palestinians living in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: NCCIA says child pornography network busted, with father allegedly involved in selling videos of his children
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Sunday claimed to have busted an international child pornography network in which a father was allegedly involved in making and selling explicit videos of his own children.

Islamabad NCCIA Additional Director Mohammad Shoaib Khan, speaking at a press conference in the capital, asserted that this was the first case in Pakistan’s history where a father was found involved in such a heinous crime against his own minor children.
The NCCIA official claimed the man was “involved in making indecent videos of his children, aged between four and five, and selling them”.

stories.title: Shadab Khan's maiden ODI century steers Pakistan into tri-series final after thrilling chase against England
summary: With the last wicket standing and Haris Rauf holding firm at the other end, Pakistan needed 27 runs when Shadab swept Gus Atkinson for six over fine leg.
Shaheen broke the stand by dismissing Curran, caught at fine leg, before Duckett reached his fifth ODI century off 104 balls — his first against Pakistan.
England then lost Will Jacks (13) to Razaullah, who took a sharp return catch for his maiden ODI wicket, while Liam Dawson (five) fell to another short ball, caught by Shadab at deep square leg.

stories.title: 6 terrorists killed, 2 soldiers martyred during Dera Ismail Khan IBO: ISPR
summary: Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). “Owing to [the] meticulous conduct of operation by security forces, six India-sponsored khawarij were sent to hell,” ISPR said.

Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed terrorists, who “remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities against the security forces and law enforcement agencies, as well as the killing of innocent civilians”, the ISPR statement noted.
Earlier this month, security forces killed eight terrorists during an IBO in DI Khan, state media reported, citing security sources.

stories.title: The nuclear danger at sea
summary: At the Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference a week later, retired Lt-Gen Khalid Kidwai, also an adviser to the National Command Authority, reinforced the warning, saying Pakistan would review its options if India sought to impose a strategic imbalance.

A supersonic nuclear-capable missile crossed the border in peacetime; India waited nearly two days before acknowledging it and did not accept Pakistan’s call for a joint inquiry, raising the risk of escalation.
As India’s posture changes, Pakistan will take the measures necessary to safeguard its sovereignty and strategic balance.

stories.title: How Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump
summary: The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump’s frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv’s supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward.
Angered by Zelensky’s defiance, Trump on Oct 9 announced a deal to buy diesel from Moscow, issuing a temporary general license that allows Russian diesel to reach the global market.
At talks in Oslo on October 20, Ukraine presented new proposals, and Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner repeated Trump’s demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian diesel refineries.

stories.title: Students across country to get 500,000 Chromebooks over 2 years, announces PM Shehbaz
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday launched a scheme under which the government would distribute 500,000 Chromebook laptops to students nationwide over two years.

He addressed the launch ceremony in Islamabad of the Prime Minister’s Youth Chromebook Scheme, a nationwide initiative to distribute 500,000 Chromebooks equipped with MiFi internet connectivity to deserving students and high achievers.

The prime minister stressed that empowering the nation’s youth with modern tools was vital to helping them compete globally, while expressing gratitude to Tokyo Technology Care Foundation (TTCF) for partnering in the Chromebook initiative.

stories.title: Israeli strike on Gaza university kills 3; another 4 Palestinians killed in other attacks
summary: An Israeli strike on a university in Gaza City killed three people on Sunday, staff and a local hospital said, while the civil defence agency reported four others killed elsewhere in the territory.
Earlier this week, Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four people in the Gaza Strip on Thursday.
At least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza in Israeli airstrikes since the ceasefire, according to the territory’s health officials, while Israel says four soldiers have been killed.

stories.title: New leave policy for Islamabad Police ensures weekly off for all personnel
summary: ISLAMABAD: The capital’s police have introduced a new leave policy to ease difficulties faced by officers and officials in obtaining leave and ensure, for the first time, that all personnel get at least one day of weekly rest, it emerged on Sunday.

According to an order issued by the Islamabad inspector general (IG), dated Oct 23 and available with Dawn, the policy delegates leave-sanctioning powers to officers at different levels and supersedes all previous instructions, including the leave policy issued in 2022.
This screengrab from the order shows the delegation of powers for sanctioning leave by various Islamabad Police officials, according to rank.

stories.title: Brazil chooses between Lula and Bolsonaro in nail-biter vote
summary: Brazil held its breath on Sunday as voters went to the polls to decide between leftist leader Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva or his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.

It is the final electoral battle for Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday and is hoping to pull off a dramatic turnaround after coming in second to the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro in the first round of voting.
The day after After his first-round blow, Lula revamped his social media strategy and even bought his first cellphone.

stories.title: Jhang DC removed over use of Pera vehicle for 'non-serious purposes' in jeep rally: CM Maryam
summary: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said on Sunday that Jhang Deputy Commissioner Babar Sahib Din was being removed immediately over the recent use of an official vehicle of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (Pera) in a jeep rally, terming it a breach of discipline.
DG Khan directed the DCs to retrieve or withdraw Pera vehicles from “any unauthorised allocation”.
The chief minister had also directed the authorities concerned to upgrade Pera’s internal intelligence and whistleblower system.

stories.title: 7 killed as jeep plunges down mountain slope on outskirts of Muzaffarabad
summary: MUZAFFARABAD: Seven people, including a father and his two sons, were killed when a passenger jeep plunged down a mountain slope on the outskirts of Muzaffarabad on Sunday, officials said.
According to a police report, the jeep fell approximately 1,000 to 1,500 feet below the road.
In May, four people, including two women, were killed and two others injured after a passenger jeep plunged hundreds of feet into a rocky streambed in the same area.

stories.title: Potential resumption of war with Israel, US will not change Iran's positions: Araghchi
summary: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that a potential resumption of war with Israel and the United States would not change his country’s positions.

Iran has claimed control over the strait since the outbreak of the war and has regularly targeted vessels that attempt crossing without its authorisation — moves strongly opposed by Washington and countries in the region.

In June, Iran agreed with the United States to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, laying out a pathway to a permanent settlement of the conflict, only for the deal to later unravel as each side accused the other of violating it.

stories.title: Pak-US reset?
summary: As for Pakistan-US ties, three developments seem to have contributed to the recent thaw.
Pakistan acknowledged America’s positive role.
What matters most is making the best use of the recent thaw in Pakistan-US ties while preserving our other key relationships, including with China.

stories.title: Japan to simulate cyberattacks as PHP flaws roil global internet
summary: Japan said on Friday ​it would set up a team to simulate cyberattacks using AI to identify weaknesses in technology systems as ‌organisations scramble to curtail risks from flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet.
Highlighting the extent of the disruption, Japan's third-largest mobile carrier, SoftBank, said on Friday ​it was suspending its emergency alert system for mobile users.
Companies including brokerage Nomura, lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, airline ANA and East Japan Railway (JR East) temporarily suspended some internet services as part of emergency measures.

stories.title: PHP foundation 'under-funded' with one full-time staff member, director says
summary: The discovery of two ​serious flaws in PHP this week set off a global scramble to ‌keep websites safe from hackers, showing just how critical the three-decade-old open-source programming language is to the internet.

While Web security company Cloudflare has reported millions of hacking attempts, Barron said the foundation had no ​evidence hackers were able to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were disclosed, or ​on sites that have been patched.
It helped researchers find the flaws, which had been present for a decade, and Barron ​said it made programmers ​more efficient.

stories.title: Hina Javed murder case: In open letter to Punjab CM, victim's family again expresses mistrust in police probe
summary: Her husband and their domestic worker were arrested as Hina’s family accused them of murdering her while her father-in-law was questioned as part of the investigation.
The family requested CM Maryam to look into the case file in detail and see the evidence linking Hina’s husband “to the murder being ignored from day one”.

I will also meet the family personally.” Last month, the Punjab government constituted a three-member high-powered committee to review the investigation into the murder, in which Hina’s husband and domestic servant have been sent on judicial remand.

stories.title: PCB releases Sufiyan Moqim from tri-series squad, adds Maaz Sadaqat as cover
summary: In a brief statement, the PCB said Sufiyan had been released from the squad “keeping in view the nature of Lahore pitches” and would return to domestic cricket.
An occasional left-arm orthodox spinner, Maaz had initially been left out of the tri-series squad.
The updated squad, led by Shaheen Shah Afridi, now includes Maaz as Pakistan continue their campaign in Lahore ahead of the final on Oct 31 at the same venue.

stories.title: 'Not a single tree' will be cut down to upgrade Islamabad's F-9 Park, interior minister assures residents
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday assured the residents of Islamabad that “not a single tree” will be cut down during the planned upgradation of the city’s F-9 Park.
In a post on X, the minister shared an Instagram video of an Islamabad resident requesting that if the park were to be developed, more greenery be planted instead of concrete buildings.

The CDA maintained that only paper mulberry trees were removed as they had been causing pollen allergies, and Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry assured lawmakers that a greater number of trees would be planted in the coming months.

stories.title: Wall St week ahead earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
summary: Read: Among AI crowd, some investors position for slower hyperscaler spending growth Three other hyperscalers, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, headline a packed week of quarterly results, including about one-third of S&P 500 companies.
"Next week, ⁠you have a lot more tech earnings, and right now the market is taking a discerning eye as it relates to all the spending that goes along with artificial intelligence," Giorgi ​said.
Fed expected to pause on rates, for now Quarterly reports next week from chip companies Intel and Sandisk also could influence ​the AI trade.

stories.title: Civil society rejects plan to build Qayyumabad-Karachi Port elevated corridor
summary: The relationship between the government and the people should be built on trust.
Syed Jamal Macdi, a DHA resident, said the government seems to be spending so much money at the cost of the people and the environment. “The port anyway comes under the federal government.

Rasha Tarek, a KCF member and resident of Clifton Block 5, said that Clifton has schools, community spaces such as parks, Boat Basin, the food street, etc. “An elevated corridor will not let Clifton stay the same,” she said.

stories.title: Kundi says K-P cannot function without Centre's cooperation
summary: Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday said improved relations with the federal government were a welcome development for the province, stressing that K-P could not function without the centre’s cooperation.
Speaking to the media after attending a gathering in Swabi, the governor said the province’s problems could only be resolved through joint efforts with the federal government.
The governor said the media had every right to offer constructive criticism, adding that positive criticism helped improve institutional performance.

stories.title: Mohatta Palace to host ninth Sindh Literature Festival
summary: The ninth edition of the Sindh Literature Festival (SLF) will take place at the historic Mohatta Palace in Karachi on November 21 and 22, 2026, bringing together literature, culture, history and the stories that connect communities across Sindh.

The announcement marks the return of the festival for its ninth edition, continuing an initiative that has provided a platform for writers, poets, scholars, artists and readers to engage with Sindh’s diverse cultural traditions.
These editions demonstrated the festival’s continuing interest in connecting literary expression with the wider social, historical and cultural experiences of Sindh.

stories.title: Seven killed as passenger jeep plunges into ravine near Muzaffarabad
summary: Seven people, including two children, were killed when a passenger jeep fell into a deep ravine in Shakar Patiyan, on the outskirts of Muzaffarabad, Radio Pakistan reported.

According to rescue officials, the jeep, which was carrying grass, was travelling from Shakar Patiyan to Siri Dara when the driver lost control while navigating a difficult stretch of road, causing the vehicle to plunge into the ravine.

The incident came a day after four children from the same family were killed and four others injured when a van carrying them to a religious school plunged into a deep ravine in Azad Jammu and Kashmir's Neelum Valley.

stories.title: Netanyahu rebuked for plan to use crypto to bypass economic sanctions
summary: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces re-election this week, is drawing criticism from economists and political rivals ​after suggesting Israel could use cryptocurrency to help shield its economy from potential international sanctions.
In an interview ‌with Israel's Channel 10 on Friday, Netanyahu said he was preparing for a scenario in which broader sanctions were imposed on Israel.

Read: UK, France and Canada sanction Israeli West Bank settlements, in support for two-state solution "There could be sanctions, ​and sanctions on banks, so you need to set up a bypass economy," Netanyahu said.

stories.title: ECP proposes 12 amendments to regulate AI, curb misuse in elections
summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) proposed 12 amendments to the 2023 codes of conduct for political parties, media organisations and election observers to curb the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) during elections.

According to sources in the ECP, the draft amendments proposed five changes to the code of conduct for media organisations, five for political parties and candidates, and three for election observers.
Five amendments have been proposed for political parties and candidates to regulate their use of AI-generated material during election campaigns.

stories.title: Trump calls Obama ‘grossly incompetent’ after ex-president unloads on him at rallies ahead of US midterms
summary: Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration.

Campaigning in Michigan for El-Sayed, Obama framed the November 3 vote as a “circuit breaker” to “at least rein in some of the foolishness” of Trump’s presidency. “We got to flip that circuit breaker, bring some accountability to this government,” Obama said.
Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats.

stories.title: Putin says accusations of Russia provoking European protests are ‘clear overkill’
summary: As is known, Russia has always been accused of all mortal sins.
Putin said this points to “the weakness and inability of some leaders in European countries to take responsibility for what is happening.” “This is bad.
Because it means they do not analyse the events, do not look for the causes of what is happening, but simply shift the blame onto someone, first the US, now Russia,” he said.

stories.title: Fritz to face Musetti in Lyon title match
summary: Second-seeded Taylor Fritz drilled 15 aces while overwhelming fellow American Tommy Paul 6-3, 7-5 on Saturday to reach the final at the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes in Lyon, France.
Fils carded 17 aces and saved 7 of 10 break points but could not stop Struff, who won the final two points of the tiebreaker to win the match.
Struff had a 43-42 edge in winners and won 18 of 27 points at the net.

stories.title: Protesters clash with police over India dam project bordering China
summary: Indian protesters angry over a proposed Himalayan mega-dam, intended to counter an upstream Chinese hydropower project, have clashed with police and torched buildings, officials said.
India says the proposed dam is needed to counter China’s $167-billion Yaxia project, a likely record-breaking hydropower scheme upstream in Tibet.
India’s proposed dam, which would be by far its largest hydropower project, has drawn fierce opposition from local communities who fear the loss of their homes and land.

stories.title: Saif Ali Khan attack trial begins as nurse tells court intruder demanded INR10m
summary: The trial in the knife attack on Bollywood actor Saif Ali Khan began in Mumbai, with the first witness telling the court that the intruder had demanded INR10 million during a break-in at the actor’s Bandra residence in January 2025.
The nurse, who cared for Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan’s younger son, Jeh, identified the accused, 31-year-old Mohammad Shariful Islam, during her testimony on Friday, according to Gulf News.
According to the witness, the man subsequently attacked Khan and another member of the household staff.

stories.title: Turkish court seeks investigation into nationals allegedly involved in abuse of Gaza flotilla activists in Israel
summary: Flotilla participants describe alleged mistreatment During the hearing, complainant Osman Cetinkaya said he had joined the flotilla as a doctor to deliver medical supplies to Palestinians in Gaza.
He referred to provisional measures ordered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in proceedings concerning allegations of genocide in Gaza.
The court additionally ordered that a UN report submitted concerning allegations of genocide in Gaza be requested through the Justice Ministry.

stories.title: Apple's iPhone Duo faces early durability concerns as users report cracked screens
summary: Apple’s first foldable iPhone is facing early durability concerns after owners reported cracks in the inner display near the hinge, in some cases within hours of purchase.
However, social media posts alone cannot establish a failure rate or confirm that all reported cases share the same cause.

Another user, fenibook, reported on Friday that two cases of inner-display failure had already emerged on the phone’s launch day, adding that further reports over the following days would help establish whether the problem was more widespread.

stories.title: As actors get more physical, Bollywood embraces intimacy coordinators
summary: India's film industry, where scenes featuring nudity or sex often rely on improvisation and mutual trust, is gradually welcoming professionals tasked with choreographing intimacy to protect actors and ensure consent.

"Just like a stunt director handles a fight scene... for scenes of intimacy, we map out exactly where the hand goes and where the hair goes so nothing is left to awkward improvisation," said Aastha Khanna, one of a small but growing group of intimacy coordinators in Bollywood.
Intimacy coordinator Khanna worked to establish personal boundaries and choreograph scenes, while intimacy coach Neha Vyaso conducted workshops focused on physical dynamics and consent.

stories.title: Mona Lisa off limits as Paris shuts museums over protest fears
summary: Disappointed tourists poked their heads through ​the Louvre's locked gates on Saturday, shut off from the Mona Lisa as galleries ‌and museums across Paris closed as a precaution ahead of fresh demonstrations.
"We wanted to at least see the pyramid," 67-year-old Canadian Don Nowschuk said, referring to the museum's landmark glass entrance.
We didn't think a museum could be closed.
